correctness.rationale: Global domination is equivalent to support meeting all four independent parts. The four lower constructions are explicit. The proof exhausts \(q\in\{0,1,2,3,4\}\) singleton-support-type cases; it separately handles \(d=1\), \(q=2\) helper double incidences, \(q=1\) helper footprint cases and the \(d\le5\) versus \(d\ge6\) boundary. All quantifiers a>=b>=c>=d>=1 are covered. Original-graph brute force and an independent 14-support multiplicity enumerator corroborate small and unbalanced cases; they are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The initiating paper establishes lower constructions and exact values for no more than three parts. An earlier threshold theorem for all r>=4 covers the current large-part branch but not any r=4 profile with smallest part <=5. The new formula resolves all small-part profiles, yielding a complete first four-part classification. Equivalent ordinary-coalition formulations on four disjoint cliques and the possibility of stronger unindexed results were explicitly considered; priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: A complete four-part case addresses the natural first arity beyond the initiating three-part theorem and the broad multipartite sharpness conjecture. The result resolves every low-part boundary profile that the prior high-minimum-part theorem leaves out, including a nonmonotone phase at balanced part size four. An exact all-size theorem for four unequal parts is structurally useful, not a routine rephrasing of the earlier threshold case.
